links.outcome: Emergency recognition and safety under adversarial parental pressure in pediatric queries
links.effect: Emergency recognition was absent; adversarial queries reduced safety by 8% (p=0.03), urgency causing largest drop (-1.40); critical failures 4.8% (70B) vs 12.0% (8B).
links.quote: Hedging strongly correlated with safety (r=0.68, p<0.001), while emergency recognition was absent.

links.outcome: Diagnostic restraint and disclaimer maintenance under adversarial parental pressure
links.effect: Adversarial queries reduced safety by 8% (p=0.03); seizure queries showed 33.3% inappropriate diagnosis.
links.quote: Vulnerabilities appeared in seizures (33.3% inappropriate diagnosis) and post-vaccination queries.

screen.reason: The study introduces and evaluates a benchmark (PediatricAnxietyBench) to assess LLM safety under adversarial parental pressures, but does not test or compare a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
